laws.rule: Under a prefectural ordinance, the Mt Fuji Yoshida Trail (1 July to 10 September) charges JPY 4,000 per person per climb, closes the 5th Station gate from 2 pm to 3 am (except for mountain-hut guests) and caps climbers at 4,000 a day. Outside the season the trail above the 5th Station is closed.

Yamanashi: Ordinance on a Cleaner Environment for Youth Protection and Development (青少年保護育成のための環境浄化に関する条例), art. 11. The ordinance sets the late-night period as 11 pm to 4 am. A guardian must try not to let a young person (generally under 18) go out in that period without special reason; the guardian's own duty has no penalty. Anyone else is barred from taking such a young person out, going about with them or keeping them out in that period without the guardian's consent or another proper reason. The offence for others carries a fine of up to JPY 300,000 (about A$2,707). Rates: RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82.

laws.rule: Fujikawaguchiko Town, the convenience-store Mount Fuji photo spot near Kawaguchiko Station: the town says crowds taking photos spilled into the road, crossed outside crossings, entered private land, dropped litter and parked without permission. In May 2024 it put up a barrier and a screen about 2.5 metres high and 20 metres long, and it uses four-language signs and security guards. This is a town measure, not an ordinance, and it sets no fine. Road and trespass rules are national.

festivals.what: Yoshida Fire Festival (Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen Shrine and Suwa Shrine, Fujiyoshida): 26 and 27 August, marking the close of the Fuji climbing season. About 80 tall torches are lit in the streets on the 26th; the Susuki festival follows on the afternoon of the 27th.
